chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him (peace be upon him) while I was present, regarding a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting. He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever divorces his wife three times according to the Sunnah, then she is fully divorced from him.' He then turned to me and said: 'So-and-so does not know how to say this properly, so it does not contradict the previously narrated reports, because he only said:
Indeed, whoever divorces his wife three times according to the Sunnah, then she is fully divorced from him.

And that does not happen except by consummating the marriage with her according to what the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established in three times, upon the fixed conditions in that matter.
And whoever divorces his wife three times in one instance, the three divorces are not enacted according to what is established in the Sunnah and confirmed in the Sharia.
And he (peace be upon him) did not explicitly state that to the questioner due to a form of taqiyyah (dissimulation), and he said what serves as a reminder regarding it.

key_terms.يُوَاقِعَهَا: he consummates the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: Does a triple divorce in one sitting count as three divorces or just one according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between a triple divorce pronounced in a single sitting and the Sunnah method, which requires three separate divorces with consummation in between. He explains that the brevity of his initial answer was due to taqiyyah, while the phrase 'for the Sunnah' served as a subtle hint to the full ruling. This highlights the Shia view that talaq al-sunnah is the standard for a complete divorce, contrasting with the majority view of talaq al-khulasah.
